thread.title: US Dollar: Will we see 4 Interest Rate Hikes in 2018? 99% Probability for 3 hikes

author: James Elliot
title: US Dollar: Will we see 4 Interest Rate Hikes in 2018? 99% Probability for 3 hikes
text:
US Dollar: Will We See 4 Interest Rate Hikes In 2018? 99% Probability For 3 Hikes US Dollar: Will We See 4 Interest Rate Hikes In 2018? 99% Probability For 3 Hikes Posted by James Elliot on Feb 28, 2018 Facebook Powell’s First Testimony Lifts the US Dollar Back Over 90 - New Fed Chair Jerome Powell took centre stage and delivered a clear message. The Fed will not respond to every little wobble in the equity markets: the course of rate hikes is data dependent, and the data is strong. There may even be a fourth rate hike this year. 
The new Fed Chair Jerome Powell made his mark on the markets during the first day of the semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony. Equity markets reversed lower after a week of sustained strength and the US dollar found a bid to break back above 90. 
From this reaction you can probably guess at the tone of his comments. Equity bulls were perhaps hoping for a dovish tone and a hint the Fed may back off its course of rate hikes in light of the recent correction. Yet the message was hawkish and clear: the Fed will remain on course and there is the distinct possibility of a fourth rate hike in 2018 if the economy and inflation merit it. 
“What we’ve seen is incoming data that suggests the strengthening in the economy. We’ve seen continuing strength in the labor market. We’ve seen some data that will, in my case, add some confidence to my view that inflation is moving up to target. We’ve also seen continued strength around the globe, and we’ve seen fiscal policy become more stimulative.” 
During the Q&A Powell was quite direct and didn’t hint at any backing down if recent equity volatility were to continue. 
“The Treasury market sell-off was partially reversed largely because equities started to fall into a slide over the course of the afternoon and ended up closing at the lows of the day. This sort of disappointment by equities from a relatively upbeat assessment of macro conditions is perplexing. However, given that the markets are accustomed to a Fed that has historically leaned on the dovish side, the sell-off makes sense, in our view. Perhaps Chair Powell is not fazed by the recent volatility in risk assets as it was not brought up in today’s discussion and this could hint that the “Fed put” is lower than the 10% correction and short-lived vol spike experience a few weeks back. Considering the market reaction during and following his testimony, we will be monitoring his language, if any, on financial conditions,” reported Nomura today. 
Perhaps the equity markets will once more test Powell’s resolve. He had barely been in post when the early February crash knocked 10% off equities in a matter of weeks. Heavyweights such as Apple (AAPL) fell 16% in the largest decline since early 2016. 
So far Fed speakers have dismissed the falls, and with Apple already back at new all time highs, perhaps they were right to. The Fed have been criticized for being overly concerned with each and every market move, and perhaps Powell wants to distance himself from this. 
Even still, we can expect any change in policy to continue to be well telegraphed, a point made by RBC in their morning note, 
“If there is a concerted effort to shift expectations about the FF dot profile, our Economists think it should be pretty obvious over various Fed speeches in coming weeks. For the remainder of the week, Kashkari speaks tonight on Wages, while Powell testifies again and Dudley speaks on Trade on Thursday.” 
Fed funds are now pricing in a probability of 74% for 4 hikes, and 99% for 3 hikes in 2018, up from around 60% previously. 
This has helped the US dollar further its recovery and trade right back to the February highs, up 2.6% from the mid-month low of 88.25. Breaking above 90.55 could bring 92 where the dollar would be flat for the year and cause every short in 2018 to reconsider their position. The verdict is still out, but there is a chance for the dollar to reverse its downtrend. Advertisement James Elliot James Elliott is an entrepreneur and an independent trader.
